Afternoon cloud build-up and scattered showers typical of the summer rainy season are expected to limit solar heating and cap temperatures near the seasonal average of roughly 24–25 °C. No unusual ridge or heat-advection pattern is present to push readings higher, while the absence of strong cooling would prevent a drop to 25 °C or below. Latest model runs show only minor spread around these values, supporting the market’s heavy weighting toward 26 °C and 27 °C.

eventMetadata.context_description: The active southwest monsoon (habagat) over Luzon remains the dominant driver, with PAGASA forecasts for August 18 showing a 26–31°C range and 60% rain probability amid persistent cloud cover that reduces solar insolation and caps daytime maxima. Recent model consensus and observational trends align with trader emphasis on 28°C as the leading outcome, reflecting typical monsoon suppression of peaks below the seasonal 30–31°C average. Any temporary breaks in showers could briefly support 29–30°C readings, while sustained convection would favor 27°C or lower, consistent with the combined 95% implied probability for the top three bins. Updated PAGASA briefings and next model runs will provide the key data shifts ahead of resolution.
